4) From `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` and `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, list EVERY path that would gate checkout work — i.e. anything a checkout build would plausibly touch (order-summary, promo-code, pickup-or-delivery, product-item, display-price, theme/components, hooks like use-current-basket / use-current-customer, config/, ssr.js, routes.tsx). For each, give the tier (1 or 2) and the named owner. Be exhaustive for checkout-relevant paths only.

5) Find where the "shared/ui barrel trap" is documented. Grep for `shared/ui` across `.claude/`, `.docs/`, and `overrides/` (exclude node_modules) and report every file:line that discusses it, plus a summary of what the trap actually is. Also verify the claim by checking: does `overrides/app/components/shared/` exist? And how many files under `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` import from `app/components/shared/ui`? (count with grep -rl | wc -l).

6) Read `CODEOWNERS` and report every rule that would apply to `overrides/app/pages/checkout/`, `overrides/app/components/**`, `**/*.css.ts`, and `overrides/app/theme/**`.

7) Check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` (and any sibling in `.docs/memory/`) for what it says about checkout / cart / payment scope and which sprint they belong to. Quote the relevant lines.

Return a precise structured report with repo-relative file paths and line numbers. Do NOT write any report file — return findings as your final message text.

1	# Styling an Override Component
2	
3	How to style a component under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/theme/`.
4	Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness — a
5	different concern: that file is about not breaking SFCC's own imports, this one is
6	about what values to reach for once the component compiles). Day-to-day CSS/token
7	rules live in [css.md](./css.md); this file is the practical "what do I actually type"
8	companion.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## The hierarchy — reach for these in order
13	
14	1. **`textStyle` prop** for anything textual. `textStyle="body2"`, never a raw `fontSize`.
15	   All 22 Handover text styles are registered in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`.
16	2. **Raw `var(--zimm-*)` CSS custom properties** for colour and spacing — `color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"`,
17	   `bg="var(--zimm-color-bg-02)"`, `gap="var(--zimm-scale-m)"`. **Never** a bare Chakra/theme
18	   token string (`color="text.default"`, `gap="m"`) — even though `theme.colors`/`theme.space`
19	   ARE registered from the same Zimmermann foundations (see `theme/index.ts`'s own comment on
20	   which scales are and aren't registered) and a bare key resolves to the identical value. This
21	   is a house-style requirement, not a correctness one: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference is
22	   unambiguous at every call site, where a bare key forces a PR reviewer to check
23	   `theme/index.ts`'s registered-scale list to know whether it happens to be correct. Mechanically
24	   enforced across every recipe file by `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s "no
25	   override-component style uses a bare token key on a registered scale" test — it walks the
26	   registered recipe map only, so it cannot see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop (see
27	   that test's SCOPE note); apply the same discipline there by hand.
28	3. **A component's own theme config** — either centralized (`theme/components/<name>.ts`)
29	   or, per the co-location pattern below, beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — for
30	   anything that needs to vary by variant/size/state and isn't already a Chakra prop — see
31	   "Component-local tokens" and "Co-locating a component's theme file" below. For an
32	   interactive component with existing Chakra support (buttons, inputs, etc.), this theme
33	   config is the single source of truth — see "One canonical styling surface per component
34	   type" below.
35	4. **`sx` prop** for a one-off Chakra-prop-system gap, per [css.md](./css.md).
36	5. **Scoped `.scss`** only when `sx` genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors,
37	   keyframes) — same file, same rules as [css.md](./css.md) already documents.
38	
39	**Never**: a raw hex/px/rem/em literal in a component file — reach for the token
40	instead. The one standing exception is `zimmButton.css.ts`'s provisional height/padding
41	constants (`BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y`), pending UI-designer
42	sign-off — see Units below. Run `npm run audit:tokens` (`node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`)
43	before opening a PR that touches `overrides/app/components/**` or
44	`overrides/app/theme/components/**` — it greps for exactly this, scoped to those two paths
45	(`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.scss`, excluding `*.test.ts(x)` and `*.stories.tsx`). A match is downgraded
46	from a failure to an acknowledged exception when the surrounding comment block already
47	contains `provisional`, `pending`, `placeholder`, or an explicit `audit-allow: <reason>` —
48	the exact vocabulary this codebase already uses for its documented raw-value exceptions, so
49	existing well-commented code doesn't need a second, separately-maintained allow-list. Built
50	2026-08-23 — it is not wired into CI yet, deliberately: someone still needs to own triaging a
51	full run's worth of pre-existing findings first (a first run against this repo surfaced 14
52	genuine pre-existing violations, none touched by that session, all outside its scope to fix).
53	Note this is a *different, broader* check than `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token-key guard
54	mentioned above: that one exists and runs today (`npm run test`), but only catches a bare
55	Chakra key standing in for a zimm var — it says nothing about a raw hex/px/rem/em literal,
56	which is what `audit:tokens` is for.
57	
58	## Units
59	
60	- **`rem`** for anything that should scale with the user's root font-size / browser zoom
61	  (WCAG 1.4.4): type (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`) and spacing
62	  (`spacing.ts`'s named scale). Letter-spacing values that were specified as sub-pixel px
63	  in the source don't round to clean rem numbers, so those keep a trailing `// -0.12px`
64	  comment for traceability.
65	- **`px`** for hairline geometry that should _not_ scale: border widths, focus-ring
66	  offsets, and (for now) the provisional button-height constants in `zimmButton.css.ts` that are
67	  still pending UI-designer sign-off against Handover.
68	- **`em`** only for breakpoints (`gridSystem.ts` — deliberate, so `.zimm-grid`'s media
69	  queries shift with zoom the same way Chakra's responsive props do) and other
70	  genuinely context-relative cases. Not a general-purpose unit.
71	
72	## The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy
73	
74	`theme/foundation/colour.ts`'s primitive tier (`grey`, `ivory`, ...) is defined first as
75	plain `const`s, and the semantic/alias tier below it (`text`, `background`, `border`,
76	...) reads from those consts (`text.default: grey[900]`) instead of retyping the hex
77	value. Do the same for any new primitive/alias pair you add — two values can't disagree
78	if only one of them is ever typed.
79	
80	`zimmTokens.ts` (the `--zimm-*` CSS-var registry for `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*`
81	classes) is fully derived the same way — it imports `colors`/`spacing`/`fontSizes`/
82	`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings`/`fontWeights`/`iconSizes`/`actionSizes`/`motion`/`grid`
83	from their owning files rather than retyping values. The only literals left are the 7
84	numeric `--zimm-scale-NNN` aliases with no named-scale equivalent (`025`, `700`, `1100`,
85	`1200`, `1300`, `3500`, `4500`) — not duplicates, just Handover values with nothing to
86	derive them from. `theme/index.test.tsx`'s collision-guard tests still exist as a
87	regression net; treat a failure there as a real drift signal, not test noise.
88	
89	## One canonical styling surface per component type
90	
91	Only one place should define how a given interactive component looks: its theme config —
92	either centralized as `theme/components/<name>.ts` or, per the co-location pattern below,
93	beside the component as `<name>.css.ts` — consumed via Chakra's component (`<Button>`,
94	`<Link>` variant, etc.). Don't also give it a `.zimm-*` global class in
95	`globalStyles.ts` — a static CSS class can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/
96	`_focusVisible` states the way a Chakra theme config can, so a class "mirror" is
97	structurally incomplete from the start, and nothing stops its values from disagreeing
98	with the real theme config over time. `zimmButton.css.ts` (co-located at `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/`) is the single source of truth for
99	button styling; `globalStyles.ts` has no `.zimm-btn-*` classes — use Chakra's `<Button>`
100	for any button, not a class.
101	
102	`.zimm-*` classes remain the right tool for genuinely static, non-interactive,
103	massively-reused treatments (typography, the responsive grid, form-field layout) where
104	there's no interactive state to lose.
105	
106	## Importing an already-overridden component from a new component
107	
108	If component A (e.g. `productDetailOptions`) uses component B, and B already has an
109	override (e.g. `swatch-group`), **import B via a relative path
110	(`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path
111	(`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the
112	base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override
113	that's itself shadowing an SFCC module (see `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
114	import, which is correct for that file).
115	
116	The reason the two cases differ: the resolver that redirects
117	`@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in
118	`package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev
119	server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to
120	`node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the
121	resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run
122	correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC
123	version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your
124	override and isn't.
125	
126	**Known instance of this, not yet fixed:** `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice`
127	import uses the base path. Currently dormant only because its Storybook story exercises
128	the `CardBaseline` named export (which takes `price` as a pre-rendered node and never
129	calls `DisplayPrice`), not the default `ProductTile` bridge that actually renders it —
130	worth fixing before anything writes a story/test against the default export.
131	
132	An override component's own base-path imports (of modules it is _not_ also
133	overriding) are unaffected by this — `RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker`
134	etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them.
135	
136	## Component-local tokens
137	
138	When a component needs a spacing/sizing value that already has a `spacing.ts` /
139	`iconSizes` / etc. entry, reference that entry **as a `var(--zimm-*)` custom property**
140	— `marginBottom: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)'`, not `marginBottom: 2`, not
141	`marginBottom: '0.5rem'`, and **not** the bare key `marginBottom: 'xs'`. The bare-key
142	form resolved correctly against the registered `theme.space` and was what this section
143	used to recommend, but hierarchy point 2 above now forbids it and
144	`theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`'s bare-token guard **fails the build on it** —
145	so following the old advice inside a registered recipe breaks `npm run test`.
146	
147	See `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts` and
148	`.../footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts` for the pattern in a real recipe. The reason is
149	traceability, not parity with the base theme: a `var(--zimm-*)` reference names the
150	Figma token it came from, where a raw `2` or `'0.5rem'` names nothing. (Note these
151	recipes are deliberately namespaced `ZimmFooter*` so they do **not** inherit the base
152	SFCC `Footer` config — their values come from Figma, not from re-expressing base
153	numerics. See `recipeGuards.test.ts`'s namespacing guard.)
154	
155	**Responsive steps are explicit media queries, not Chakra's array shorthand.** A
156	co-located recipe keys them off `BP` in `theme/components/footerShared.ts`, in the form:
157	
158	```ts
159	[`@media (min-width: ${BP.tablet})`]: { gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-3xl)' },
160	```
161	
162	The array shorthand (`['2xs', '2xs', 'xs', 'xs']`) is what this section used to
163	recommend, and it would put a bare token key back at every step — the guard walks
164	responsive arrays and attributes each element to the same prop, so all four fail.
165	`footer.css.ts`'s `contentRow` and `linksInner` parts are the reference.
166	
167	When a component needs a dimension with **no existing foundation entry** (and you don't
168	have a confirmed Figma value for it), leave it inherited from the base SFCC theme rather
169	than inventing a number — don't guess at design values. Follow the precedent already in
170	`header.ts`/`zimmButton.css.ts`: if you do have to ship a placeholder value pending designer
171	sign-off, say so in a comment next to it, the same way those files already do.
172	
173	## The SFCC bridge pattern (shared components only)
174	
175	If the component is used internally by SFCC's own base components (check with `grep -r
176	"from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'"
177	node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`), its **default export must stay a
178	faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour,
179	matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness. Put
180	Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default and adds
181	brand-specific defaults, the same split `product-tile/index.tsx` (`CardBaseline`
182	name + default) and `link/index.tsx` already use. `image-gallery`, `display-price`, and
183	`swatch-group` are all shared internal SFCC dependencies. When one of them does get
184	overridden, keep its default export API-compatible and put brand styling in a theme
185	recipe rather than a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't require a second
186	export the way `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.
187	
188	**As of `7b9b5dc`, none of the three is overridden at all** — no component override, no
189	theme recipe, nothing registered for them in `theme/components/index.ts`. Verify current
190	state before relying on any of this. `protectedFiles.md` and `CODEOWNERS` list those
191	paths forward-lookingly, not descriptively. An earlier revision of this paragraph cited
192	`theme/components/imageGallery.ts` / `swatchGroup.ts` as holding their styling; neither
193	file has ever existed on any branch.
194	
195	---
196	
197	## Co-locating a component's theme file
198	
199	A component's recipe may live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
200	`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, or an organism's own
201	`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/<name>/<name>.css.ts`) instead of in
202	`theme/components/`. Either way it's still registered in
203	`overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` — Chakra resolves a recipe by the string key
204	passed to `useMultiStyleConfig`, not by file path, so co-location is purely an
205	organisational choice with no runtime difference.
206	
207	**Governance follows the file, not the folder.** `theme/components/` is Tier 2, gated to
208	the UI designer (protectedFiles.md). A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is deliberately routed
209	differently: CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule sends it to the
210	owning squad(s) only, dropping the Tier 1/2 approver requirement that the surrounding
211	directory (e.g. `header/`, `footer/`) otherwise carries. That's intentional — a co-located
212	file is for composing a component's own layout from **already-established** tokens
213	(spacing, colour, typography scale), not for authoring new raw design values. Authoring an
214	actual new token still means editing `theme/foundation/` (Tier 1) or a `theme/components/`
215	recipe that's still designer-owned (`header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `navConstants.ts` — the
216	files that remain in that directory) — both stay behind the full gate.
217	
218	> **Known inconsistency, flagged not resolved.** This paragraph used to cite `button.ts`'s
219	> `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM`/`BTN_PADDING_Y` as the designer-gated example. That file
220	> is now `ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts`, which the `**/*.css.ts` rule above
221	> routes to the squads — so those provisional, unapproved constants are **no longer
222	> designer-gated**, while still keying the app-wide `Button` recipe. The example was swapped
223	> to `header.ts` (genuinely still gated) so this paragraph stops asserting something false.
224	> Whether `zimmButton.css.ts` should be re-gated is an open governance question, not a doc
225	> fix, and is deliberately left open here.
226	
227	**Enforcement gap, partially closed:** the Tier 1/2 human reviewer was, until this rule
228	existed, the only thing catching a hardcoded hex/px/rem/em value landing in a theme file.
229	`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` (`npm run audit:tokens`, see the `Never` note above) now exists
230	and runs correctly against the real codebase — built 2026-08-23. What's still open: it is not
231	wired into CI, so it only catches something if a developer or reviewer remembers to run it —
232	removing the Tier 1/2 reviewer from co-located `.css.ts` files still removes an *automatic*
233	backstop for exactly the files most likely to need it. Wiring `audit:tokens` as a required CI
234	check on `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` is the remaining near-term follow-up, not an
235	optional nice-to-have — and per the script's own header, someone should triage a full run's
236	findings first (14 pre-existing, unrelated violations turned up the day it was built) before
237	turning it into a hard gate.
238	
239	**Cross-file shared values** (a breakpoint or provisional size needed by more than one
240	split-out file) go in a small shared module that stays in `theme/components/` — e.g.
241	`footerShared.ts`, holding the breakpoints and the one size value `footerNavColumn.css.ts`
242	and `bottomBar.css.ts` both need. Don't copy the same literal into two co-located files;
243	that's exactly the drift risk "The alias tier is a reference, not a second copy" (above)
244	already warns about.
245	
246	**Reference example:** the footer decomposition (SFCC-55 follow-up) split
247	`theme/components/footer.ts`'s 33 parts across `footer/footer.css.ts` (shell),
248	`footer/footerNavColumn/footerNavColumn.css.ts`, `footer/bottomBar/bottomBar.css.ts`, and
249	three `ui-kits/organisms/`/`ui-kits/molecules/` recipes — with `footerShared.ts` left
250	behind in `theme/components/` for the two genuinely cross-file values.
251	
252	## Known gaps (not silently dropped — logged here)
253	
254	- The f2r `zimm-product-detail-options` prototype spec includes a size-as-dropdown
255	  picker, a wishlist button, a "find in boutique" link, and description/shipping
256	  accordions. None of those exist as overrides yet, so `ProductDetailOptions` ships
257	  without them — it's colour/size swatches, quantity, and add-to-bag only.
258	- `swatch-group`'s `square`/`circle` variant functions (selected/disabled colour logic,
259	  the diagonal disabled-state gradient) are still inherited from the base SFCC theme —
260	  real visual design decisions with no Zimmermann Figma spec behind them yet.
261	- `zimmButton.css.ts`'s `BTN_HEIGHT_LG`/`BTN_HEIGHT_SM` (50px/41px) disagree with the
262	  Handover-sourced `actionSizes.height.lg`/`.md` (52px/40px) — flagged in `zimmButton.css.ts`,
263	  pending UI-designer sign-off. `BTN_PADDING_Y` (5px) has no Handover token at all —
264	  a gap to fill, not a conflict to resolve.
265	- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` is claimed by `.claude/rules/squadA.md`
266	  (draft, scope still settling) — flagged for awareness, not treated as a hard block.
267	
268	## Follow-up work (separate initiatives)
269	
270	- **Per-component CSS loading.** `globalStyles.ts`'s `.zimm-*` class registry is
271	  registered as one `theme.styles.global` block and ships on every page regardless of
272	  which classes a given page's components actually use. If component overrides start
273	  applying `.zimm-*` classNames directly for the non-interactive cases described above,
274	  only the classes a page's components actually reference should load, not the whole
275	  registry. Needs its own investigation, not scoped or estimated yet.
276	- **`globalStyles.ts` adoption is currently near zero.** Of the classes still defined
277	  there, none have a real consumer anywhere in the app today except one Storybook demo
278	  (`spacing.stories.tsx`'s `.zimm-grid` example). They're Handover-ported 1:1 and
279	  presumably _intended_ to be reused, just not adopted by any component yet — worth
280	  revisiting once component overrides actually start applying them.

110	## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
111	     2	
112	Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.
113	     4	
114	## Overrides Pattern
115	     6	
116	All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.
117	     8	
118	**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.
119	    10	
120	**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:
121	    12	
122	1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
123	2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
124	3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
125	4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**
126	    17	
127	## New vs. Override Components
128	    19	
129	- **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/` (see Overrides Pattern above).
130	- **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.
131	    22	
132	## Key Paths
133	    24	
134	- **Country/locale/currency mappings:** `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` — single source of truth for URL slugs, locales, currencies, shipping countries, Global-e flag, and boutique regions. When adding a market also update `config/sites.js`.
135	- **Contentful config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — always render locale-specific content using Contentful's native localisation fields. Gate preview/draft content behind a server-side check; never expose draft content in production.
136	- **Theme / design tokens:** `overrides/app/theme/` — `index.ts` composes the theme; brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing, sizes, motion, and the `--zimm-*` registry in `zimmTokens.ts` — Tier 1, UI Designer owned); the `.zimm-*` global classes composed from them live in `globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2); a per-component override lives either one file each in `components/` (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` — Tier 2, UI-designer gated) **or**, per the co-location pattern, beside its component as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g. `overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmButton/zimmButton.css.ts` — governed by that component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead). Either way it's registered in `theme/components/index.ts`. See [.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md](../.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md) > Co-locating a component's theme file. Note: brand fonts (Futura Round) **are** self-hosted — two faces ship from `overrides/app/static/fonts/` via `theme/fontFace.tsx`, mounted unconditionally, so they are served on every tier. See [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md) > Design System.
137	- **App shell (Header/Footer):** `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`
138	- **Header:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`
139	- **Custom components:** `overrides/app/components/custom/`
140	- **Assets:** `overrides/app/static/`, `overrides/app/assets/svg/`
141	    32	
142	## Design Source of Truth
143	    34	
144	Figma file "29 April 2026" is the **current working draft** — not a signed-off final design. Implementations based on it are client-preview builds and may need to be revised when designs are finalised. Do not treat any Figma-derived decision as confirmed without explicit sign-off.
145	    36	
146	Desktop prototype at zimm-prototype.vercel.app is AI-generated and desktop-only — also not a signed-off final design.
147	    38	
148	## Header Layout (based on draft Figma, subject to change)
149	    40	
150	Two rows: top bar (nav + icons) and logo row. Implemented in `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, with Chakra theme overrides split across `overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts`.
151	    42	
152	**Logo**: uses `BrandLogo` from the icons package (PWA default with the svg file replaced). The Z.IMMERSE variant has not been implemented yet.
153	    44	
154	**ListMenu active-state gotcha**: `listMenuTriggerLinkActive` is JS-spread _after_ `listMenuTriggerLink` on the same `<Link>` element. Any `_after` key in the active style entirely replaces the base `_after` object — all CSS properties must be repeated, not just the overriding ones.
155	    46	
156	**Icons deferred**: Boutique, Contact, Newsletter (HPC-015) — icon assets not provided yet.
157	    48	
158	**Base functionality retained**: All hooks, the account popover, wishlist, store locator, and all existing props are unchanged. Only layout and visual style changed so far.
159	    50	
160	## Contentful Content Type Management
161	    52	
162	Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are
163	authored in code as one organization-scoped **Environment Template** and installed into
164	each environment — Contentful's current recommended mechanism, replacing an earlier
165	per-environment sync pipeline. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and
166	team-safe.
167	    58	
168	**Key paths:**
169	    60	
170	- `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` — assembles every content type in the definitions directory into one `EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`
171	- `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — validates then installs the template's current version into one target environment
172	- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `footerConfig.js`), the sole source of truth for its fields (including `localized`/`required`/`validations`)
173	    64	
174	**To register a new content type:**
175	    66	
176	1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
177	2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`
178	3. Run `npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>` for each environment in the promotion chain
179	    70	
180	**To run it:**
181	    72	
182	```
183	npm run sync:contentful
184	npm run install:contentful -- --target dev
185	```
186	    77	
187	Requires `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` (scope:shared) and `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` — a personal token tied to your own Contentful account (scope:personal, never pushed to the centrally-shared GitHub Environments store, but fine to hold locally). Both live in your local, gitignored `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold them, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running). Get the management token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.
188	    79	
189	Both scripts are idempotent — safe to re-run. Field deletion during an install is opt-in
190	(`--delete-deleted-fields` on `install:contentful`), off by default.
191	    82	
192	**Relationship to the React component:**
193	Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.
194	    85	
195	**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding content-type entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.
196	    87	
197	## Path Aliases
198	    89	
199	Configured in four places (keep in sync):

# Checkout Override Constraints — Zimmermann PWA

## 1) `.claude/rules/overrides.md` — **DOES NOT EXIST**

This is the headline finding. `find . -name "overrides*.md" -not -path "*/node_modules/*"` returns nothing. `.claude/rules/` contains: `components.md`, `conventions.md`, `css.md`, `frozenFiles.md`, `overrideStyling.md`, `protectedFiles.md`, `squadA.md`, `squadB.md`, `tagging.md`, `testing.md`, `typescript.md`.

**`overrides.md` is referenced as an existing authority in 5 places and every one is a dead link:**

| Referencing file:line | What it claims lives there |
|---|---|
| `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:4` | "Cross-references [overrides.md](./overrides.md) (module-replacement correctness…)" |
| `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:112` | "…the base path is exactly what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) requires _inside_ an override" |
| `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md:179` | "…matching what [overrides.md](./overrides.md) already requires for correctness" |
| `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md:60` | routes reader to `overrideStyling.md` (this one resolves) |

So the canonical module-replacement rules a checkout override needs are **not written down anywhere as a rule file**. What exists is scattered across `AGENTS.md`, `.docs/architecture.md`, and `overrideStyling.md`. I reconstructed the rules from those plus the actual resolver source.

### The `ccExtensibility` resolver — how it actually works (from source, since no rule file documents it)

`node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`:
- **:45** globs `overrides/**/*.*` — *every* file with an extension, no allowlist.
- **:58-62** builds `extendsHashMap` keyed on the path with the **extension stripped**, splitting on the last `.` (or on `index`). Regex: `item.split(/(index(?!(\.[^.]*\.))|\.(?!([^.]*\.)))/)`. The negative lookaheads exist so `index.tsx` and `index.test.tsx` in the same dir don't collide.
- **:74-94** `findFileFromMap` — an import of `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout` is stripped to `app/pages/checkout`, looked up extension-free, and redirected to the overrides file.

**File-extension rule (the real one):** because the map is keyed extension-free, `overrides/app/pages/checkout/index.tsx` shadows base `index.jsx` transparently. `config.js:85` confirms the entry-point probe order: `['.js', '.jsx', '.ts', '.tsx']`. `config.js:159` sets webpack `resolve.extensions: ['.ts','.tsx','.js','.jsx','.json']`. There is **no `overridesDir` extension allowlist in `package.json`** — see §2.

### Base path vs relative path — the rule, and it is inverted between two cases

From `overrideStyling.md:106-134` (verbatim, :109-113):

> "**import B via a relative path (`'../swatch-group'`), not the SFCC base path (`'@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/swatch-group'`)** — even though the base path is exactly what [overrides.md] requires _inside_ an override that's itself shadowing an SFCC module"

- **Inside an override that shadows an SFCC module**, importing a module you are *not* also overriding → **base path** (`overrideStyling.md:132-134`: "`RecommendedProducts`, `Seo`, `QuantityPicker` etc. have no local override to miss, so the base path is simply correct for them").
- **A new component importing an already-overridden component** → **relative path**.

### What breaks in Storybook / Vitest (`overrideStyling.md:117-124`, verbatim)

> "the resolver that redirects `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` imports to `overrides/` (`ccExtensibility` in `package.json`, read by a webpack plugin) only runs in the **real app build** — dev server and production. `.storybook/main.js` aliases that package straight to `node_modules` and `vitest.config.ts` doesn't touch it at all, so neither loads the resolver. A base-path import of an already-overridden component will build and run correctly in the shipped app, but silently render/test the **unstyled base SFCC version** in Storybook and Vitest — the story or test looks like it's exercising your override and isn't."

**I verified both halves of this claim:**
- `.storybook/main.js:32` — `'@salesforce/retail-react-app': path.resolve(__dirname, '../node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app')`. Confirmed: straight to node_modules, no override resolution.
- `vitest.config.ts:32-60` — `resolve.alias` has `~`, `app`, and several `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` subpath entries. **No `@salesforce/retail-react-app` entry at all.** Confirmed.

This is the single highest-risk trap for a checkout override: base checkout has 32 files under `partials/` that import each other via base paths. Every one of those you override but leave imported by base path will silently test/story the base version.

### Known traps

1. **Dormant instance, unfixed** (`overrideStyling.md:126-130`): `product-tile/index.tsx`'s `DisplayPrice` import uses the base path. Dormant only because the story exercises the `CardBaseline` named export.
2. **SFCC bridge pattern** (`overrideStyling.md:173-186`): if SFCC's own base components import your component internally, its "**default export must stay a faithful, undecorated port**" — full prop surface, same `forwardRef`. Brand styling goes behind a **named export**. Check with `grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`.
3. **Copy-first, then stop** (`AGENTS.md:134`, `architecture.md:120-125`): copy → convert to TS → `npx tsc --noEmit` → add temporary `console.log('[overrides] …')` markers → **stop and present to user**. "Never skip this step or bundle it silently with functional changes."
4. **`ListMenu` `_after` spread gotcha** (`architecture.md:154`) — pattern-relevant if checkout reuses spread style objects: "Any `_after` key in the active style entirely replaces the base `_after` object — all CSS properties must be repeated."

### The "extends"/"overridesDir" config semantics

`config.js:56` normalises `overridesDir` to a leading-slash posix path. `config.js:68-73` throws if `extends` and `extendable` overlap. `config.js:95` — app entry point is forced to `<overridesDir>/app/main`. `config.js:153-155` passes `{extends: [EXT_EXTENDS], overridesDir: EXT_OVERRIDES_DIR, projectDir: cwd}` into the plugin.

## 5) The "shared/ui barrel trap"

### It is NOT documented in `.claude/` or `.docs/` — at all

`grep -rn "shared/ui" .claude/ .docs/ overrides/ AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md` returns **zero hits in `.claude/` and zero in `.docs/`**. Every hit is under `overrides/`, and the explanatory ones are **inline code comments**, not rules.

**Files that discuss it (as opposed to just importing from it):**

| File:line | What it says |
|---|---|
| `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:30-32` | "Imported directly from @chakra-ui/react, not the shared/ui barrel: that barrel's `useBreakpointValue` re-export is an untyped .jsx passthrough — same reasoning as product-detail/index.tsx's own import of this hook." |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:30-32` | "that barrel's `useBreakpointValue` re-export (`shared/ui/useBreakpointValue/index.jsx`) is an untyped .jsx passthrough, so a generic type argument on it fails to compile — same reasoning ui-kits files already use for importing hooks straight from '@chakra-ui/react' (see zimmDrawer/index.tsx)" |
| `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.test.tsx:47-49` | "@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui re-exports Chakra UI. Stubbed with plain HTML so no real Chakra theme/provider is needed." — then `vi.mock(...)` of the whole barrel |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.test.tsx:8` | same `vi.mock` of the barrel |
| `overrides/app/components/list-menu/list-menu-popover.test.tsx:14-19` | The key one: the transitive-chain trap. Mocking at the exact boundary "(**not the whole shared/ui barrel**) is the smallest surface that stops the chain" |
| `overrides/app/components/header/rightBar/index.tsx:228, 255, 435` | "chakra.div used intentionally: Flex/Box from shared/ui don't reliably apply `__css` — use chakra factory directly (footer pattern)." |
| `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmSearchInput/zimmSearchInput.css.ts:7` | "The clear button is an IconButton from shared/ui (same pattern as header icon buttons)." |
| `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/staticProductHeader.tsx:12` | "`Breadcrumb`, `PromoCallout` and `shared/ui` above have no [override]" — the base-path-is-correct case |

Closest thing in the rule files is `.claude/rules/testing.md:75` — "**Known gap: `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel…" — the same class of defect for a *different* barrel.

### What the trap actually is — three distinct failure modes

1. **Untyped `.jsx` passthrough breaks generics.** `shared/ui/useBreakpointValue/index.jsx` is plain JSX with no types, so `useBreakpointValue<T>(...)` won't compile. Workaround in use: import hooks straight from `@chakra-ui/react`, components from the barrel.
2. **`__css` doesn't reliably apply.** `Flex`/`Box` from the barrel drop `__css`; `header/rightBar` uses the `chakra.div` factory directly in three places instead.
3. **Transitive module-eval explosion under Vitest.** Per `list-menu-popover.test.tsx:13-19`: a static import pulls `list-menu-content.jsx` → `links-list` → `link` → `use-multi-site` → base contexts barrel, "a `.js` file with raw JSX Vite's import-analysis can't parse under Vitest." The barrel is a broad surface, so mocking *it* over-mocks; the rule is to mock the narrowest boundary that breaks the chain.

### Verification of the claims

- **`overrides/app/components/shared/` does NOT exist.** `ls` → "No such file or directory". So the barrel is *never* shadowed — a base-path import of `shared/ui` is always correct, and every one of the ~30 import sites above is fine. This is exactly the `overrideStyling.md:132-134` case.
- **Files under `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` importing `app/components/shared/ui`: `212`** (`grep -rl … | wc -l`).

**Implication for checkout:** 212 base files route through this barrel. Because `overrides/app/components/shared/` doesn't exist, the barrel itself is not a module-replacement hazard — but any checkout test that renders a base partial will hit failure mode 3, and the established remedy is a narrow `vi.mock` at the offending boundary, not a barrel-wide mock.
